s6244: Under the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, a driver involved in a road traffic accident leaving the scene, or moving a vehicle involved in the accident from the scene, except in cases provided for by law, results in:
s6242: Administrative detention for up to 3 months
s6243: A fine of GEL 200 or administrative detention for up to 15 days
s6245: According to Part 1 of Article 123 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, a driver involved in a road traffic accident leaving the scene, or moving a vehicle involved in the accident from the scene, except in cases provided for by law, results in a fine of GEL 250.
s6248: Under the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, failing to obey an order to stop the vehicle given by a police officer who ensures the safety of road users and supervises compliance with the traffic rules results in:
s6247: A fine of GEL 500 or suspension of the right to drive for 3 years
s6249: According to Part 2 of Article 123 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, failing to obey an order to stop the vehicle given by a police officer who ensures the safety of road users and supervises compliance with the traffic rules results in a fine of GEL 300.
s6252: Under the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, a driver exceeding the set speed limit by more than 15 km/h results in:
s6253: According to Part 1 of Article 125 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, a driver exceeding the set speed limit by more than 15 km/h results in a fine of GEL 50.
s6255: Under the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, a driver exceeding the set speed limit by more than 15 km/h, which leads to an emergency situation or holds up traffic, results in:
s6254: Administrative detention for up to 30 days
s6256: According to Part 4 of Article 125 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, the offence provided for in Part 1 of this Article (a driver exceeding the set speed limit by more than 15 km/h) that leads to an emergency situation or holds up traffic results in a fine of GEL 300.
s6259: Under the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, a driver exceeding the set speed limit by more than 15 km/h, which leads to minor damage to a vehicle, cargo, the road, a road or other structure, other property, or minor bodily injury to a person, results in:

s6258: A fine of GEL 500 or administrative detention for up to 15 days
s6260: According to Part 5 of Article 125 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, the offence provided for in Part 1 of this Article (a driver exceeding the set speed limit by more than 15 km/h) that leads to minor damage to a vehicle, cargo, the road, a road or other structure, other property, or minor bodily injury to a person, results in a fine of GEL 500.
s6262: Under the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, a driver breaking the rules on road signs or road markings, towing, using external lights, the horn or hazard warning lights, learner driving, driving in a residential zone or the traffic rules, the priority of route vehicles and/or driving animal-drawn vehicles, or taking part in group riding on motorcycles or other vehicles, where this holds up traffic or endangers traffic safety, results in:
s6263: According to Part 6 of Article 125 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, a driver breaking the rules on passing pedestrian crossings, road signs or road markings, towing, using external lights, the horn or hazard warning lights, learner driving, driving in a residential zone or on the road, the priority of route vehicles and/or driving animal-drawn vehicles, or taking part in group riding on motorcycles or other vehicles, where this holds up traffic or endangers traffic safety, results in a fine of GEL 20.

s6264: Suspension of the right to drive for up to 15 days
s6266: According to Part 6² of Article 125 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, breaking the rules on the positioning of vehicles on the carriageway, moving off and/or manoeuvring results in a fine of GEL 50.
s6270: Under the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, driving a vehicle with an identification sign fixed in breach of the rules results in:
s6267: A fine of GEL 50 for the driver or the company
s6268: A fine of GEL 50 for the driver
s6269: A fine of GEL 100 for the driver or the company
s6271: According to Part 6³ of Article 125 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, driving a vehicle with an identification sign fixed in breach of the rules results in a fine of GEL 50 for the driver or the company.
s6274: Under the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, obstructing a vehicle that has priority results in:
s6272: Deprivation of the right to drive for 1 year
s6273: A fine of GEL 100 or deprivation of the right to drive for 3 months
s6275: According to Part 7 of Article 125 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, breaking the rules on passing a traffic officer's or a traffic light's prohibiting signal, not complying with a priority sign ("Give way", "No entry without stopping") or a prohibitory sign ("No entry", "No vehicles"), breaking the rules on overtaking, passing through intersections or crossing railways, or obstructing a vehicle that has priority, results in a fine of GEL 50.
s6279: Must a driver be aware of factors that affect how they drive (for example tiredness, lack of sleep, taking medicines, drinking alcohol, etc.)?
s6276: Yes, regardless of which vehicle they are driving
s6277: Only a driver of a motor-powered vehicle must
s6278: Only a driver of a bus or truck who regularly carries passengers or goods must
s6280: According to paragraph 5 of Article 21 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the driver must know the traffic rules and must also be aware of factors that affect how they drive, for example tiredness, lack of sleep, taking medicines, drinking alcohol, etc.
s6284: Which of the following factors does NOT affect how a driver drives?
s6285: According to paragraph 5 of Article 21 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the driver must know the traffic rules and must also be aware of factors that affect how they drive, for example tiredness, lack of sleep, taking medicines, drinking alcohol, etc.
s6289: If a driver feels tired while driving, it is advisable to:
s6286: Stop the vehicle and rest, and if possible let another driver take the wheel
s6290: According to subparagraph "j" of paragraph 10 of Article 25 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, when driving on the road, the driver must bear in mind the following: if the driver feels tired while driving, it is advisable to stop the vehicle and rest, and if possible let another driver take the wheel.
s6291: May a person drive a vehicle while under the influence of a narcotic drug that they took for medical purposes, as prescribed by a doctor?
s6292: According to paragraph 15 of Article 21 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, it is prohibited to drive a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol, drugs or psychotropic substances, or under the effect of a medicine that slows reactions and reduces attention.
s6293: May a person drive a vehicle while under the influence of a psychotropic substance that they took for medical purposes, as prescribed by a doctor?
s6294: Is it prohibited to hand over a vehicle to be driven by a person under the influence of a narcotic drug that they took for medical purposes, as prescribed by a doctor?
s6295: According to paragraph 4 of Article 20 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, it is prohibited to hand over a vehicle to be driven by a person who is under the influence of alcohol, drugs or psychotropic substances.
s6296: Is it prohibited to hand over a vehicle to be driven by a person under the influence of a psychotropic substance that they took for medical purposes, as prescribed by a doctor?
s6299: Is it prohibited for a person to drive a vehicle while under the effect of medicines that slow reactions and reduce attention?
s6297: It is not prohibited if the medicines were taken for medical purposes, as prescribed by a doctor
s6298: It is not prohibited if the person drives taking the necessary precautions
s6301: Is it prohibited to hand over a vehicle to be driven by a person who is under the effect of medicines that slow reactions and reduce attention?
s6300: It is not prohibited if the medicines were taken for medical purposes, as prescribed by a doctor
s6302: According to paragraph 4 of Article 20 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, it is prohibited to hand over a vehicle to be driven by a person who is under the influence of alcohol, drugs or psychotropic substances. According to paragraph 15 of Article 21 of the same Law, it is prohibited to drive a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol, drugs or psychotropic substances, or under the effect of a medicine that slows reactions and reduces attention.
s6305: Is it prohibited for a person to drive a vehicle while under the influence of drugs?
s6303: It is not prohibited if they took the drug for medical purposes, as prescribed by a doctor
s6304: It is not prohibited if they notify the relevant police service in advance
s6308: Is it prohibited for a person to drive a vehicle while under the influence of psychotropic substances?
s6306: It is not prohibited if they drive taking the necessary precautions
s6307: It is not prohibited if the substance was taken for medical purposes, as prescribed by a doctor
s6310: Is it prohibited for a person to drive a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol?
s6309: It is not prohibited if the driver is in Georgia as part of international traffic
s6314: How does alcohol affect a driver's reactions?
s6313: It has no effect on reactions
s6315: Drinking alcohol lengthens the driver's reaction time.
s6319: Why is it dangerous for a driver under the influence of drugs to drive a vehicle?
s6316: Drug intoxication causes all the effects listed in this question
s6317: Only because the reaction time of a driver under the influence of drugs is longer
s6318: Only because a driver under the influence of drugs cannot properly judge the situation on the road
s6320: Driving a vehicle while under the influence of drugs is dangerous, because the driver's reaction time is longer and they cannot properly judge the situation on the road.
s6325: Which of the following can impair a person's ability to drive a vehicle?
s6321: Any of the circumstances listed in this question
s6322: Only severe tiredness or lack of sleep
s6323: Only taking a medicine that slows reactions and reduces attention
s6324: Only intoxication with alcohol, drugs or psychotropic substances
s6326: A person's ability to drive a vehicle can be impaired by taking a medicine that slows reactions and reduces attention, by severe tiredness or lack of sleep, and by intoxication with alcohol, drugs or psychotropic substances.
s6330: Before starting to overtake, the driver must make sure:
s6327: Only that the driver of the vehicle ahead in the same lane has not signalled an intention to overtake another vehicle
s6328: Only that the lane they intend to move into is clear for a sufficient distance, and that the difference in speed between the two vehicles allows overtaking in a sufficiently short time
s6329: Only that no driver of a vehicle behind has started to overtake
s6331: According to subparagraphs "a", "b" and "c" of paragraph 3 of Article 34 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, before starting to overtake, the driver, without breaching the requirements of paragraph 2 of Article 20 and Article 32 of this Law, must make sure that: a) no driver of a vehicle behind has started to overtake; b) the driver of the vehicle ahead in the same lane has not signalled an intention to overtake another vehicle. It is prohibited to overtake a vehicle that is overtaking or going around an obstacle; c) they can overtake without endangering or obstructing other road users. They must also make sure that the lane they intend to move into is clear for a sufficient distance and that the difference in speed between the two vehicles allows overtaking in a sufficiently short time.
s6334: If a route vehicle has stopped or slowed down before an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, drivers of other vehicles in the neighbouring lanes may continue:
s6332: Only after making sure there is no pedestrian in front of the stopped route vehicle
s6333: Without changing speed, because a pedestrian must not step out from in front of a stopped vehicle until they have made sure no vehicle is approaching
s6335: According to paragraph 9 of Article 25 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, if a route vehicle has stopped or slowed down before an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, drivers of other vehicles in the neighbouring lanes may continue only after making sure there is no pedestrian in front of the stopped route vehicle.
s6338: A driver who intends to reverse must make sure that:
s6336: They can carry out the manoeuvre without endangering or obstructing other road users
s6337: Other road users give way to them as the one with priority
s6340: On a road with at least two lanes for traffic in the same direction, may a driver stay in the lane they used for the first overtaking if they will have to start another overtaking as soon as, or shortly after, they return to the lane they used before?
s6339: Yes, if they first make sure this will not obstruct a faster vehicle coming up behind them
s6341: According to paragraph 6 of Article 34 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, on a road with at least two lanes for traffic in the same direction, a driver who, after finishing overtaking, would have to start another overtaking as soon as, or shortly after, returning to the lane they used before in order to comply with paragraphs 10-12 of Article 31 of this Law, may stay in the lane used for the first overtaking to carry out this manoeuvre, provided they first make sure this will not obstruct the driver of a faster vehicle coming up behind them.
s6345: Except when leaving the road to the left, a driver who realises that the driver behind intends to overtake must:
s6342: Keep as close as possible to the right-hand edge of the carriageway and not speed up
s6343: Move to the far left of their side of the road and slow down
s6344: Move to the right-hand edge of the carriageway and speed up
s6346: According to paragraph 12 of Article 34 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a driver who realises that the driver behind intends to overtake must, except in the case provided for in subparagraph "b" of paragraph 7 of Article 32 of this Law, keep as close as possible to the right-hand edge of the carriageway and not speed up. According to subparagraph "b" of paragraph 7 of Article 32 of the same Law, before turning right or left to enter another road or adjacent territory, without breaching the requirements of paragraph 2 of Article 20 of this Law and paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, if the driver intends to leave the road to the left, the vehicle must keep as close as possible to the centre line of the carriageway (on a two-way road) or to the left-hand edge of the carriageway (on a one-way road).
s6350: Before leaving a motor vehicle, the driver must make sure:
s6347: That they have taken all the necessary precautions to prevent a road traffic accident, and also all the measures to prevent the motor vehicle from being used without permission
s6348: Only that they have taken all the measures to prevent the motor vehicle from being used without permission
s6349: Only that they have taken all the necessary precautions to prevent a road traffic accident
s6351: According to paragraph 8 of Article 37 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a driver must not leave their vehicle without taking all the necessary precautions to prevent a road traffic accident; in addition, in the case of a motor vehicle, all measures must be taken to prevent it from being used without permission.
s6355: Before driving onto a pedestrian crossing, the driver must make sure that:
s6352: They will not be forced to stop on it
s6353: No other vehicle is coming across the crossing from the opposite direction
s6354: The surface of the crossing is not icy
s6356: According to paragraph 6 of Article 25 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a driver must not drive onto a pedestrian crossing without first making sure that they will not be forced to stop on it.
s6359: A driver who intends to make any manoeuvre must start it only after making sure that:
s6357: It will not endanger road users behind, ahead or to the side of them, travelling in the same or the opposite direction, taking into account their position, direction of travel and speed
s6358: It will not endanger only vehicles behind or to the side of them, taking into account their position, direction of travel and speed
s6360: According to paragraph 1 of Article 32 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a driver who intends to make any manoeuvre must start it only after making sure that it will not endanger road users behind, ahead or to the side of them, travelling in the same or the opposite direction, taking into account their position, direction of travel and speed.
s6364: Must a driver involved in a road traffic accident make sure that no one has been injured or killed in the accident?
s6361: Yes, but only if they are a doctor
s6362: No, if they make sure an ambulance is called
s6363: No, if the road traffic accident was not their fault
s6365: According to subparagraph "b" of paragraph 1 of Article 27 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a driver involved in a road traffic accident must: b) make sure that no one has been injured or killed in the road traffic accident.
s6369: If the driver of a truck ahead of your vehicle intends to turn right into a street with a narrow carriageway, you should bear in mind:
s6366: Only that, because of the vehicle's large turning radius, it may move to the left just before the turn
s6367: Only that it may stop during the turn to give way to pedestrians
s6368: Only that it will slow down sharply
s6370: If the driver of a truck ahead of your vehicle intends to turn right into a street with a narrow carriageway, you should bear in mind that, because of the vehicle's large turning radius, it may move to the left just before the turn; it may also slow down sharply, and it may stop during the turn to give way to pedestrians who are crossing.
s6373: For safety, is it advisable for the driver of a vehicle fitted with head restraints to make sure before setting off that they and the passengers have their head restraints supporting the back of the head?
s6374: Before setting off, the driver of a vehicle fitted with head restraints must make sure that they and the passengers have their head restraints supporting the back of the head.
s6378: If the view of an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing is partly blocked by a vehicle stopped in front of it, a driver approaching the crossing may continue:
s6375: Only after making sure there is no pedestrian on the crossing or stepping onto it
s6376: Without changing speed, whatever the situation on the crossing
s6379: If the view of an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing is partly blocked by a vehicle stopped in front of it, a driver approaching the crossing may continue only after making sure there is no pedestrian on the crossing or stepping onto it.
s6382: At a stop with a raised boarding platform, stepping onto the carriageway to board a vehicle is allowed:
s6380: Only after the vehicle has stopped
s6381: In advance, as soon as the vehicle comes into view
s6383: According to paragraph 13 of Article 24 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, at a stop with a raised boarding platform, stepping onto the carriageway to board a vehicle is allowed only after the vehicle has stopped. After getting off the vehicle, a pedestrian must leave the carriageway immediately.
s6386: In a built-up area, the driver of a route bus is starting to pull away from a stop. The driver of the car must:
s6384: Slow down and stop if necessary
s6385: Continue without changing speed, as the one with priority
s6388: Which vehicle's driver must give way when driving in the direction of the arrow outside a built-up area, if the driver of the route vehicle is starting to pull away from the stop?
s6387: The driver of the route vehicle
s6389: According to paragraph 1 of Article 41 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, subject to the requirements of paragraph 4 of Article 33 of this Law, in a built-up area, to make it easier for route vehicles to move, drivers of other vehicles must slow down and stop if necessary so that the route vehicle can carry out the manoeuvre needed to pull away from the stop. After signalling the intention to move off with the turn indicator, the driver of a route vehicle must take the precautions needed to prevent a road traffic accident and may move off only after making sure that other vehicles are giving way. According to paragraph 1 of Article 32 of the same Law, a driver who intends to make any manoeuvre must start it only after making sure that it will not endanger road users behind, ahead or to the side of them, travelling in the same or the opposite direction, taking into account their position, direction of travel and speed.
s6390: In this situation, which driver has priority if the driver of the yellow car is moving off after letting passengers out and the driver of the black car is stopping to pick up passengers?
s6391: According to paragraph 1 of Article 32 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a driver who intends to make any manoeuvre must start it only after making sure that it will not endanger road users behind, ahead or to the side of them, travelling in the same or the opposite direction, taking into account their position, direction of travel and speed.
s6392: According to paragraph 5.14 of Chapter 5 (Special regulation signs) of Annex 1 to the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, road sign 5.14 "Lane for route vehicles" marks a road on which route vehicles travel in a specially reserved lane in the same direction as the general flow of traffic. The sign applies to the lane above which it is placed. A sign placed on the right-hand side of the road applies to the far right-hand lane of the carriageway. According to paragraph 1.23 of Chapter 1 (Horizontal markings) of Annex 2 to the same Law, road marking 1.23 marks a special lane reserved for route vehicles. According to paragraph 3 of Article 41 of the same Law, on a road with a lane for route vehicles marked with road signs 5.11, 5.13.1, 5.13.2 and 5.14, other vehicles are prohibited from driving and stopping in that lane. If this lane is separated from the rest of the carriageway by a broken marking line, other vehicles must move into this lane when turning. Entering this lane at such places is also allowed when joining the road and when letting passengers on or off at the right-hand edge of the carriageway, provided this does not obstruct route vehicles.
s6393: Which of the stopped vehicles has priority when moving off in the direction of the arrow, if the driver of the route bus is moving off from a marked stop in a built-up area?
s6397: Stopping vehicles is prohibited, if this obstructs route vehicles, within how many metres of a purpose-built stopping place for route vehicles or taxis, or, if there is none, of the route vehicle or taxi stop sign?
s6398: According to subparagraph "b.g" of paragraph 6 of Article 37 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, stopping a vehicle is prohibited anywhere it may create danger, including within 15 metres of a purpose-built stopping place for route vehicles or taxis, or, if there is none, of the route vehicle or taxi stop sign, if this obstructs those vehicles.
s6402: Waiting for route vehicles is allowed:
s6399: Only on a boarding platform raised above the carriageway, or, if there is none, on the sidewalk or shoulder
s6400: Only on the sidewalk or shoulder
s6403: According to paragraph 13 of Article 24 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, waiting for route vehicles and taxis is allowed only on a boarding platform raised above the carriageway, or, if there is none, on the sidewalk or shoulder.
s6407: Drivers who intend to pass a route vehicle at a properly marked stop on their side of the road must:
s6404: Slow down and stop if necessary, so that passengers can get on or off the public transport vehicle safely
s6405: Speed up so as to pass quickly and not hold up passengers getting on and off the public transport vehicle
s6406: Stop at the shoulder and not move off until the public transport vehicle moves on
s6410: If there is no boarding platform, waiting for route vehicles and taxis is allowed:
s6408: Only on a traffic island in the middle of the carriageway
s6409: Only at the far right-hand side of the carriageway
s6411: According to paragraph 13 of Article 24 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, waiting for route vehicles and taxis is allowed only on a boarding platform raised above the carriageway, or, if there is none, on the sidewalk or shoulder.
